issues.description: Resource IDs are interpolated directly into URL paths, allowing slashes or query strings in IDs to change the requested endpoint.
Retry logic only handles HTTP responses and does not retry or wrap transient httpx transport, connection, or timeout exceptions.
Batch creation silently drops malformed result entries and does not verify that every submitted task received a result.
Retry delays are uncapped, so a huge Retry-After header or repeated backoff can hang callers for an unreasonable time.
Pagination response shape is not validated, malformed items are silently skipped, and repeated cursors can loop indefinitely.
batch_create materializes the entire iterable before chunking, contradicting the any-number-of-tasks API and risking high memory use.
Model parsing coerces missing or wrong-typed API fields instead of validating them, which can hide upstream contract violations.
Literal fields such as status, state, batch status, and verdict are not runtime-validated against their allowed values.
TaskCreate accepts a mutable payload directly, so frozen dataclass instances can still be mutated through nested dictionaries.
max_attempts is not validated, so zero or negative values produce confusing no-request behavior.
The package advertises typed models but does not include a PEP 561 py.typed marker for downstream type checkers.
Tests cover happy paths and basic HTTP errors but miss ID escaping, transport retries, malformed responses, and incomplete batch results.
